hero.headline: SpaceX valuation reaches $2.6 trillion, briefly surpasses Amazon
hero.body:
SpaceX's valuation reached $2.6 trillion, temporarily exceeding Amazon's market capitalization as the company's shares began trading publicly. The rocket and satellite manufacturer's value increased by $1 trillion since its shares started trading on Friday.

The valuation milestone marks a significant shift in the aerospace industry, with SpaceX becoming one of the most valuable companies in the world. The company operates multiple divisions including rocket launches, the Starlink satellite internet service, and spacecraft manufacturing. Its recent public trading debut has attracted substantial investor interest.

The $1 trillion increase in just several days of trading represents one of the fastest valuation surges for a newly public company. SpaceX's diverse portfolio includes commercial satellite launches, government contracts with NASA and the Department of Defense, and its growing Starlink internet constellation serving customers globally.

The company's founder Elon Musk has positioned SpaceX as a leader in reusable rocket technology and satellite communications. The Starlink division alone operates thousands of satellites providing internet service to remote areas. SpaceX also holds contracts for NASA's Artemis moon program and regularly launches astronauts to the International Space Station.

While SpaceX briefly exceeded Amazon's market value, both companies' valuations fluctuate based on trading activity. The aerospace company's public debut represents a shift from its previous status as a privately held corporation, opening its ownership to public investors for the first time. The strong initial market response indicates investor confidence in the company's commercial space ventures and satellite internet business.

cards.headline: Iran Announces Nuclear Talks to Begin Friday After Initial US Agreement
cards.body:
Iran's foreign minister announced that new talks on nuclear arms and sanctions relief would begin Friday, following the signing of an initial agreement to end hostilities with the United States. President Trump stated he hopes to put the conflict in the rearview mirror.

The agreement marks a significant shift after a military conflict that began on February 28. According to Iranian officials, the deal includes provisions requiring Israel to withdraw from Lebanon. The framework emerged from negotiations conducted in Oman, where diplomatic efforts stretched across multiple rounds over the past year.

The talks leading up to this agreement faced significant challenges. Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner led the US negotiating team, though their approach drew criticism from regional observers. A Gulf diplomat with direct knowledge of the talks expressed frustration with their methods, describing them as unconventional and poorly resourced. The US team included Michael Anton, a political philosopher with no specialization in nuclear policy, and lacked the technical expertise that characterized previous diplomatic efforts. In comparison, the Obama administration sent 10 senior officials from four departments to Iran talks in Vienna in 2009.

The final round of talks occurred in Geneva on February 26, where Iran presented a seven-page written offer for a new agreement. Witkoff's request to keep a copy of the proposal was denied, a decision that later became a point of contention. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has indicated he hopes the truth about what occurred during final negotiations will eventually become public.

Iran bears some responsibility for the breakdown as well. The country has not published its written offer despite calls from within Iran to do so. According to some accounts, misunderstandings about Iran's nuclear program, including the purpose of the Tehran Research Reactor and the scope of Iran's planned nuclear capabilities, contributed to the deterioration of talks.

Kushner acknowledged that a deal could have been achieved that was superior to the 2015 Obama nuclear agreement. The compressed timeline for negotiations also hindered progress. On February 17, Witkoff allocated only three and a half hours for talks with Iran while simultaneously meeting with Ukrainian officials, leaving limited time for meaningful discussion given the indirect nature of the negotiations.

The upcoming talks face significant obstacles. Both countries must navigate domestic political pressures while addressing fundamental disagreements over Iran's nuclear capabilities and regional influence. Inside Iran, opposition to further negotiations with the United States has emerged, with protesters outside the foreign ministry demanding no return to talks. The initial agreement provides a foundation for further discussions, but reaching a comprehensive settlement will require substantial concessions from both sides on issues that have divided them for decades.

cards.headline: FBI says group planned White House UFC event attack with drones and snipers
cards.teaser: Federal authorities detailed an alleged plot to attack a UFC event at the White House using explosive drones and snipers.
cards.body:
Federal authorities have unsealed court documents detailing an alleged plot to attack a UFC event scheduled at the White House using explosive drones and snipers, according to newly released government filings.

The Justice Department has announced charges against five men in connection with the conspiracy. According to the unsealed court documents, the group allegedly expressed grievances about government corruption, the handling of Epstein-related files, and data centers.

At least three suspects have been identified in the investigation, including a teenager. One of the suspects, Tycen Proper of Ohio, waived a court appearance in Columbus as his case progressed through the federal system.

The Trump administration is planning to hold the UFC event on the White House lawn on Sunday, marking the president's 80th birthday. The government has billed the event as a celebration of the United States' 250th anniversary. Dana White, CEO of the UFC, previously stated that the event was Trump's idea.

Federal investigators disrupted the alleged plot before any attack could be carried out. The specific details of how authorities first became aware of the conspiracy have not been disclosed by the FBI.

The UFC event has drawn criticism from various quarters. Marjorie Taylor Greene, a former Republican congresswoman who previously supported Trump, expressed concerns about the location and use of taxpayer funds. She stated that while she enjoys watching UFC fights, she does not believe they belong on the White House lawn and questioned whether American taxpayer dollars should fund the event.

A legal challenge to the event was also mounted. Attorneys from the Public Integrity Project, a nonprofit organization, filed a lawsuit attempting to prevent the UFC fight from taking place. However, on Friday a federal judge ruled that the event could proceed as planned.

Public opinion on the event has been mixed. A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted earlier this month found that only 16 percent of Americans considered the event appropriate for the White House.

The investigation and charges represent a significant security concern for the presidential residence and the planned gathering. The alleged plot involving both drone technology and sniper positions would have posed serious threats to attendees and the facility itself.

The cases remain ongoing, with additional details expected to emerge as the legal proceedings continue through the federal court system. Authorities have not released comprehensive information about all the charges each suspect faces or the complete evidence gathered during the investigation.

cards.headline: Trump Offers Ukraine Support at G7 Summit With Conditions Attached
cards.teaser: President Trump signaled potential renewed focus on Ukraine at the G7 summit, but indicated support would come with financial or strategic requirements.
cards.body:
At the G7 summit in France, Trump told allied leaders that the United States has no direct involvement in the Ukraine war. He indicated he may reimpose sanctions on Russian oil as part of a broader strategy. European leaders, including French President Macron and Ukrainian President Zelensky, pressed Trump to maintain Western support for Ukraine against Russian aggression.

The discussion marks a shift in Trump's focus after recent weeks centered on Iran, where he had signed a new agreement. Trump's conditional offer signals potential stronger U.S. engagement on Ukraine, though his approach remains tied to specific conditions.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Africa Could Become Worst on Record, Health Officials Warn
cards.teaser: The Africa CDC chief warned the current Ebola outbreak could become the worst in history if infection rates do not flatten soon.
cards.body:
Health officials are warning that the Ebola outbreak could become the worst on record if infection rates don't decline. Containment could take up to a year without a significant drop in new cases, according to the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The outbreak has already killed more than 170 people, with cases rising across affected regions in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Healthcare systems in multiple countries have been strained by the ongoing crisis.

cards.headline: Russian Warship Fires Warning Shots at UK Yacht in English Channel
cards.teaser: A Russian frigate fired warning shots near a UK-flagged yacht in the English Channel, prompting an investigation by British defense officials.
cards.body:
A Russian frigate fired warning shots near a British yacht in the English Channel on Tuesday. The retired couple aboard the vessel told BBC Newsnight they had attempted to signal a course change before the shots were fired. Russia confirmed the warship discharged the warning shots, describing them as necessary to avert a collision in international waters.

Britain's Defense Ministry launched an investigation into the incident, which occurred near UK territorial waters. The encounter underscores existing tensions between Russia and Western nations regarding naval operations in European waters, as Russian military vessels regularly transit the English Channel, a critical shipping route connecting the Atlantic Ocean and North Sea.

cards.headline: China Restricts Citizens' Access to Global Markets to Keep Capital Domestic
cards.body:
China has introduced new restrictions on how individuals can engage with global financial markets, part of a broader effort to keep capital within the country's borders. The measures limit Chinese citizens' ability to invest in foreign assets and participate in international markets, marking an expansion of existing capital controls.

The restrictions come as Chinese authorities seek to stabilize domestic markets and prevent capital flight. By constraining pathways for individuals to move money overseas, Beijing aims to ensure that household savings and investment funds remain circulating within the domestic economy. The government has increasingly prioritized financial stability and control over capital flows in recent years.

China already maintains strict capital controls, including limits on how much currency residents can exchange annually and restrictions on cross-border transfers. The new measures tighten these existing frameworks, closing loopholes that some investors had used to access foreign stocks, bonds, and other assets. Enforcement mechanisms have also been strengthened to monitor compliance.

The policy reflects ongoing tensions in China's economic management as authorities balance growth objectives with financial security concerns. Capital outflows have historically accelerated during periods of domestic economic uncertainty or when returns on foreign investments appear more attractive than domestic options. By limiting these exits, officials hope to channel more private capital toward Chinese companies and assets.

The restrictions may affect foreign financial institutions operating in China and could reduce participation by Chinese investors in global markets. International asset managers and exchanges that had cultivated Chinese clients may see reduced activity. The measures also signal Beijing's continued willingness to prioritize state control over economic liberalization, even as it seeks to attract foreign investment into China through other channels.

cards.headline: FBI Disrupts Plot to Attack White House UFC Event With Snipers and Drones
cards.teaser: Federal authorities uncovered a planned attack on a UFC event at the White House using long-range weapons and aerial devices.
cards.body:
Five men have been charged in connection with an alleged plot to attack a UFC event at the White House using snipers and drones, according to Justice Department announcements. Newly unsealed court filings reveal the group expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centers.

The FBI intervened before any attack could occur. Court documents detailed the group's planning and the coordinated nature of the proposed assault, which would have involved attacks from multiple positions using both sniper rifles and unmanned aircraft.

cards.headline: Canada Asks Some New Citizens to Surrender Citizenship Certificates
cards.teaser: Canadian officials are reviewing thousands of citizenship applications and requesting some recipients return their certificates.
cards.body:
The government told some people who received citizenship certificates under the Lost Canadians program to surrender their documents pending further review. The Lost Canadians are individuals who believed they were entitled to citizenship through family connections but faced legal barriers. Thousands had sought Canadian citizenship under provisions meant to address historical gaps in citizenship law.

The minister responsible said lost Canadians must prove a link to Canada in each generation. The review process has created uncertainty for people who received citizenship certificates and began building lives as Canadian citizens. The government has not specified how many certificates are under review or what criteria will determine who retains citizenship.

cards.headline: European Leaders Shift to Cooperative Tone With Trump at G7 Summit
cards.teaser: After years of strained relations, European leaders adopted a more conciliatory approach with President Trump at the G7 gathering in France.
cards.body:
President Trump attended the G7 summit in France, where French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated him on a new Iran agreement. Trump met with fellow G7 leaders, Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, and heads of state from Qatar and UAE during the summit's first full day.

The Iran peace framework and discussions about Ukraine cooperation created a notably different atmosphere compared to previous G7 meetings. Trump expressed hope to move past the war in Ukraine, signaling a potential shift in approach to the conflict.

cards.headline: Two hospital workers shot in Delaware, one killed; shooter remains at large
cards.teaser: Two workers at Wilmington Hospital in Delaware were shot Tuesday evening, leaving one dead and one injured.
cards.body:
Two workers at Wilmington Hospital in Delaware were shot Tuesday evening, with one killed and another injured. The shooting occurred inside the facility, prompting authorities to place the hospital on lockdown as they searched for the suspect. The injured worker received medical treatment at the hospital.

Law enforcement secured the area while hospital staff and visitors sheltered in place. The investigation remained active as police worked to locate the shooter and gather details about the incident and those involved.

cards.headline: Mississippi police kill one-year-old child during shoplifting response
cards.teaser: A police officer in Mississippi shot and killed a one-year-old child after opening fire on a vehicle during a shoplifting call at a Walmart.
cards.body:
A one-year-old boy was killed in Senatobia, Mississippi, after a police officer shot at a vehicle while responding to a shoplifting call at a Walmart. The officer opened fire on the car, striking the child. A witness reported seeing women carrying diapers during the incident.

The child died from the gunshot wounds. Authorities have not disclosed what prompted the officer to fire at the vehicle or whether anyone else in the car was injured.

cards.headline: B-52 bomber plunged nearly a mile per minute before fatal crash
cards.teaser: Early data shows a B-52 bomber on a test flight descended at nearly a mile per minute before crashing at Edwards Air Force Base, killing eight people.
cards.body:
A Boeing B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in the Mojave Desert, California during a test flight, killing all eight crew members aboard. The aircraft plunged into a fiery explosion that produced thick plumes of smoke visible across the base, located roughly 100 miles northeast of Los Angeles.

The US Air Force launched an investigation into the crash that officials said could take up to six months to complete. Early data showed the bomber descended at a rate of nearly one mile per minute before impact.

cards.headline: Louisiana faces flash flooding as potential tropical storm approaches
cards.teaser: Louisiana is experiencing dangerous flash flooding as the state prepares for what forecasters say could become Tropical Storm Arthur.
cards.body:
Dangerous flash flooding continued across Louisiana as the state braced for a weather system that could strengthen into Tropical Storm Arthur. Heavy rainfall has already caused flooding in parts of the state, creating hazardous conditions.

Forecasters are monitoring the system's development, though it has not yet been officially designated as a tropical storm. Residents in affected areas have been advised to prepare for additional flooding and possible storm impacts as the weather system moves through the region.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges 15 people with impeding immigration enforcement in Minnesota
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged 15 people with conspiracy, alleging they obstructed immigration agents during enforcement operations in Minnesota.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice charged 15 people in Minneapolis with conspiracy to impede or injure federal officers during an immigration enforcement operation earlier this year. U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen and Homeland Security Investigations special agent Michael McCarthy announced the charges at a press conference Tuesday.

Prosecutors allege the defendants were part of Minneapolis-based groups that actively opposed law enforcement during the immigration crackdown. The charges have drawn criticism from civil rights advocates who contend the prosecution targets lawful protest activity, while the Justice Department maintains the allegations involve actual interference with federal law enforcement duties.

cards.headline: Newsom says Justice Department is investigating him and his wife
cards.teaser: California Governor Gavin Newsom told allies that the Justice Department is investigating him and his wife, Jennifer Siebel Newsom.
cards.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom said the Justice Department has opened an investigation into him and his wife, Jennifer Siebel Newsom. The governor's team briefed allies in Congress about the probe, which Newsom has characterized as politically motivated. Vice President Kamala Harris said she was not surprised by the investigation, stating that the administration is targeting political opponents.

The specific focus of the investigation into Jennifer Siebel Newsom has not been fully detailed publicly. Newsom has suggested the probe is retaliatory, using it as an opportunity to criticize the administration. The Justice Department has not publicly commented on the investigation.

cards.headline: Yum Brands Sells Pizza Hut Chain for $2.7 Billion
cards.teaser: The struggling restaurant chain will be acquired by LongRange Capital and Yum China after years of declining performance.
cards.body:
Yum Brands is selling Pizza Hut for $2.7 billion to a partnership involving private equity firm LongRange Capital and Yum China. The sale marks the end of Yum's ownership of the pizza chain, which has struggled with outdated stores and intensifying competition in the pizza market.

The divestment allows Yum Brands to concentrate on its other restaurant chains, including KFC and Taco Bell. Pizza Hut has faced prolonged difficulties, including plans to close 250 U.S. restaurants as it grapples with changing consumer preferences and rival competitors.

cards.headline: Dow Crosses 52,000 as Oil Prices Drop While Tech Stocks Decline
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average reached a new milestone even as technology shares fell and the S&P 500 declined.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average reached 52,000 for the first time following a decline in oil prices. The drop came after President Trump announced a U.S.-Iran agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway, a key shipping route.

Lower oil prices benefited companies in transportation and manufacturing sectors that dominate the Dow. However, technology stocks faced selling pressure during the same session, pulling down the broader S&P 500 and Nasdaq indexes.

cards.headline: SpaceX Valuation Reaches $2.6 Trillion, Briefly Surpassing Amazon
cards.teaser: The newly public rocket company became one of the world's most valuable firms in its first days of trading.
cards.body:
Elon Musk's SpaceX has overtaken Amazon to become the world's fifth most valuable company, just days after its initial public offering. The rocket company's valuation surged to $2.97 trillion at its peak following strong investor demand for its shares.

The milestone coincided with SpaceX's agreement to acquire Cursor, an AI-powered coding startup, for $60 billion. The deal reflects the company's strategy to capitalize on artificial intelligence technology alongside its core space exploration business.

cards.headline: Rivian Lays Off Hundreds After Launching New SUV Model
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker cut approximately two percent of its workforce days after introducing a new product.
cards.body:
Rivian has cut hundreds of workers as part of a restructuring initiative aimed at achieving profitability. The layoffs follow the start of R2 deliveries for the company's new electric SUV model.

The company recently adjusted its profitability timeline to prioritize investments in autonomous driving technology. The job cuts represent an effort to streamline operations while scaling production to reach profitability goals.

cards.headline: Meta CTO Says Employee Morale Near All-Time Low
cards.teaser: Andrew Bosworth acknowledged internal discontent following organizational changes and mandatory AI initiatives.
cards.body:
Meta's Chief Technology Officer Andrew Bosworth stated that employee morale is approaching its worst levels in company history. The admission came amid internal criticism of recent organizational restructuring and mandatory participation in AI development hackathons.

Employees have expressed dissatisfaction with new AI-focused policies and the aftermath of layoffs that reduced headcount across the company. The morale issues represent a challenge for Meta as it attempts to reorganize around artificial intelligence development while maintaining productivity.

cards.headline: Trump administration moves to block Clean Air Act lawsuit over xAI data center turbines
cards.teaser: The administration seeks to halt an NAACP lawsuit claiming xAI operates gas turbines for its Grok data center without required permits.
cards.body:
The Trump administration filed to block a lawsuit brought by the NAACP alleging that xAI operates gas turbines at its Grok data center without proper Clean Air Act permits. The lawsuit centers on whether the company obtained necessary environmental approvals before installing the turbines to power its artificial intelligence operations.

The NAACP lawsuit claims xAI uses the gas turbines without securing the permits required under federal clean air regulations. The legal challenge targets the data center infrastructure supporting Grok, xAI's artificial intelligence system. The administration's intervention represents its opposition to the environmental enforcement action against the AI company.

cards.headline: Anthropic pauses token-based billing plan for Claude Agent SDK
cards.teaser: The AI company halted a billing change originally scheduled for Monday that would have substantially increased costs for heavy users of its agent development tools.
cards.body:
Anthropic postponed the implementation of token-based billing for its Claude Agent SDK, reversing a pricing change that was set to take effect Monday. The new billing model would have significantly raised expenses for power users developing applications with the software development kit.

The company described the action as a pause rather than a cancellation, leaving open the possibility of implementing similar pricing changes in the future. The Claude Agent SDK allows developers to build autonomous AI agents using Anthropic's language models. The original billing restructure would have charged based on the number of tokens processed rather than the previous pricing model.

cards.headline: Apple to move Hide My Email feature to new domain, potentially reducing privacy protection
cards.teaser: The company will relocate anonymously generated email addresses to a different domain in the coming weeks, changing how the privacy feature operates.
cards.body:
Apple plans to transfer its Hide My Email privacy feature to a new domain within the next several weeks. The service currently generates anonymous email addresses that forward messages to users' actual inboxes, shielding their real addresses from websites and services.

The domain change could reduce the feature's effectiveness at protecting user privacy, though Apple has not detailed the specific technical modifications. Hide My Email allows users to create unique, random email addresses for different services and websites, preventing companies from tracking users across platforms through their email addresses. The feature is available to iCloud Plus subscribers.

cards.headline: Scientists detect wind from Milky Way's central black hole for first time
cards.teaser: Astronomers identified wind emanating from Sagittarius A, the supermassive black hole at the galaxy's center, filling a gap in observations.
cards.body:
Scientists detected wind blowing from Sagittarius A, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy. The discovery represents the first confirmation of this feature, which researchers had expected to find based on observations of other black holes but had not previously observed from the galaxy's central black hole.

The detected wind carved out a cavity measuring three light years across. Researchers measured the wind traveling at approximately 30 percent of the speed of light. Black hole winds occur when material falling toward a black hole generates powerful outflows of gas and radiation that push matter away from the immediate vicinity of the black hole.

cards.headline: Cockroaches carry thousands of bacterial genome fragments in their cells
cards.teaser: Research shows that horizontal gene transfer between species extends beyond microbes to more complex organisms like cockroaches.
cards.body:
Cockroaches carry thousands of pieces of bacterial genomes within their cells, according to new research on cross-species gene transfer. The finding demonstrates that horizontal gene transfer, the movement of genetic material between different species, occurs in organisms beyond single-celled microbes.

Horizontal gene transfer typically involves bacteria and other microorganisms exchanging genetic material. The presence of bacterial DNA fragments in cockroach genomes suggests this process happens more broadly in nature than previously documented. Scientists identified the bacterial genetic sequences integrated into the insects' cellular material, showing genetic exchange between vastly different types of organisms.

cards.headline: Qualcomm develops chips for AI wearables including jewelry and camera-equipped earbuds
cards.teaser: The chipmaker is working on over 40 AI wearable devices as CEO signals the company expects wearables to replace smartphones as the primary computing platform.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon announced the company is developing chips for more than 40 different AI wearable devices, including jewelry, camera-equipped earbuds, pins, and watches. The executive stated the chipmaker is positioning itself for a future where wearables replace smartphones as the dominant computing platform.

The company introduced two products aimed at powering the next generation of wearable technology. Qualcomm's investment in wearable processors reflects its assessment that consumer computing will shift away from handheld phones toward devices worn on the body. The product lineup includes chips designed for diverse form factors ranging from small jewelry pieces to more traditional wearable categories like smartwatches.

---

hero.headline: Mbappe scores twice as France opens World Cup with win over Senegal
hero.body:
Kylian Mbappé scored twice as France defeated Senegal 3-1 in their opening Group I match of the 2026 World Cup, delivering an impressive performance that showcased the attacking prowess of the tournament favorites.

Mbappé's brace proved decisive in securing the victory, with his goals coming at crucial moments during the match. After a sluggish first-half display, France transformed their performance in the second period, with Mbappé breaking through just after the hour mark after receiving a superb pass from Michael Olise. He added his second goal in the closing stages of added time, cementing France's dominance as the match wore on.

The 27-year-old's two-goal haul holds particular significance for French football. His 58th international goal moves him ahead of Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading scorer, a milestone achieved during what many regard as the prime years of his career. On the World Cup stage specifically, Mbappé has now scored 14 goals across his tournament appearances.

Olise's playmaking abilities also shone throughout the contest, with the midfielder proving instrumental in France's attacking flow. The performance demonstrated the quality that has led defender Lucas Hernandez to claim France possess "the best attack in the world," featuring Mbappé as captain alongside Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé and other attacking talent.

France's victory came after a concerning first half that raised questions about their approach under manager Didier Deschamps. The coach has long been criticized for his conservative tactics, though his track record of reaching back-to-back World Cup finals and a Euros final during his 12-year tenure validates his pragmatic philosophy. Recent friendlies against Brazil and Colombia suggested Deschamps might be willing to embrace a more expansive style, and this performance against Senegal indicated that balance may have been found.

While Senegal mounted a late challenge and managed to score, they ultimately could not breach France's defensive organization. France's defense remains a cornerstone of their setup, with only four European nations conceding fewer qualifying goals than Les Bleus.

The opening victory places France in a strong position to advance from their group as they pursue another World Cup title. Mbappé's record-breaking performance sets the tone for what many expect to be a formidable tournament campaign from the favorites, combining the attacking flair that has defined their recent matches with the defensive solidity that has underpinned their success under Deschamps.

cards.headline: England defeats Ireland despite injury scare to captain Sciver-Brunt
cards.teaser: England won by four wickets at the T20 World Cup, but captain Nat Sciver-Brunt left the field with calf tightness.
cards.body:
England maintained their World Cup campaign with a four-wicket victory over Ireland in Southampton, successfully chasing down 119 despite a mid-innings wobble. The team recovered from 35 for three to complete the chase with 15 balls remaining.

Captain Nat Sciver-Brunt top-scored with 48 runs before retiring hurt with the calf injury that has troubled her throughout the summer. She will undergo assessment ahead of England's next match against Scotland at Headingley on Saturday.

cards.headline: Haaland scores for Norway after goalkeeping error by Iraq
cards.teaser: Erling Haaland benefited from a major mistake by Iraq goalkeeper Jalal Hassan during World Cup play.
cards.body:
Erling Haaland netted his second goal of the match against Iraq after a glaring error from goalkeeper Jalal Hassan. The mistake handed the Norway striker one of the easiest chances of the World Cup.

The goal showcased a significant blunder from Hassan, who was caught out by Haaland's movement during the Group stage encounter.

cards.headline: Tortorella will not return as Golden Knights head coach
cards.teaser: John Tortorella's tenure with the Vegas Golden Knights has ended after a short period as head coach.
cards.body:
John Tortorella will not return as head coach of the Vegas Golden Knights. The announcement follows what players described as a brief stint with the team.

The coaching change puts the Golden Knights in search of new leadership. The decision affects the Western Conference playoff picture, with division rivals responding to the news. Tortorella's departure marks the end of his time with the franchise after joining the organization.

cards.headline: Ghana's Partey to miss World Cup opener after visa denied
cards.teaser: Thomas Partey will sit out Ghana's first World Cup match after Canadian officials rejected his visa appeal.
cards.body:
Thomas Partey will miss Ghana's opening World Cup match after an appeal against a visa denial was turned down. Canadian officials declined to grant Partey entry, with reports indicating he misled authorities about a previous arrest.

The decision prevents Partey from joining his national team for their first game of the tournament. Ghana will need to adjust their lineup without the midfielder available for selection.

cards.headline: Scotland's Dykes prepares for World Cup match against Morocco
cards.teaser: Striker Lyndon Dykes will face Morocco as Scotland looks to build on his record of team success when he scores.
cards.body:
Lyndon Dykes has reached a major tournament with Scotland after a lengthy journey to the international stage. The striker does not score frequently, but Scotland has a winning record in matches where he finds the net.

Dykes will take the field against Morocco in Scotland's World Cup campaign. The forward brings a direct style of play to the Scottish attack as they compete in the group stage.

cards.headline: VAR declines penalty for France after Mbappe challenge
cards.teaser: Video review officials chose not to award France a penalty when Kylian Mbappe went down under Sadio Mane's tackle.
cards.body:
France did not receive a penalty kick after video assistant referees reviewed a challenge on Kylian Mbappe by Sadio Mane. The decision left French players surprised during their match against Senegal.

Referees observing the World Cup called the VAR call unexpected. The play occurred during France's 3-1 victory, with officials determining the contact did not warrant a penalty despite the review process.

hero.headline: Rapper Mystikal Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison After Guilty Plea in Rape Case
hero.body:
Louisiana rapper Mystikal pleaded guilty to third-degree rape on Tuesday in connection with charges stemming from his 2022 arrest. The 55-year-old artist, whose legal name is Michael Tyler, now faces up to 20 years in prison following the plea deal entered in a state courthouse outside Baton Rouge.

Tyler was originally charged with more serious offenses including first-degree rape, simple robbery, domestic abuse battery and false imprisonment, to which he had pleaded not guilty. Had he been convicted on those initial charges, he would have faced mandatory life imprisonment. The guilty plea to the lesser third-degree rape charge was part of an agreement that significantly reduced the severity of the case against him.

According to reports from local news outlets, the alleged victim told investigators that Tyler raped her, beat her and choked her. She also claimed he took her phone and car keys to prevent her from leaving and then forced her to send him money through the Cash App payment platform. Tyler's sentencing hearing was tentatively scheduled for June.

Mystikal rose to prominence in 2000 with the global hit "Shake Ya Ass" and went on to receive two Grammy nominations. The track gained additional cultural prominence through its appearance in the film "About a Boy," which starred Hugh Grant, Toni Collette and Nicholas Hoult. His debut album reached the top of the Billboard 200 chart.

However, this latest case adds to a troubling history of criminal convictions. In 2004, Tyler was sentenced to six years in prison after being found guilty of sexual assault and extortion involving his hairstylist, a conviction that required him to register as a sex offender. In 2012, he was jailed for three months following an arrest on a misdemeanor domestic abuse charge. More recently, in 2017, authorities charged him with rape and kidnapping, though those charges were ultimately dropped.

The guilty plea on Tuesday came ahead of a scheduled trial date set for March 30. This case reflects broader discussions about accountability within the entertainment industry regarding sexual violence. Tyler had attempted a career comeback in recent years with new music releases and select performances, efforts that now come to an end with this lengthy prison sentence, which will extend well into his later years.

cards.headline: Hayley Kiyoko Makes Directorial Debut With Film Adaptation of Her Viral Song
cards.teaser: Pop singer Hayley Kiyoko directed a feature film adaptation of her 2015 viral hit "Girls Like Girls."
cards.body:
In 2015, Hayley Kiyoko released "Girls Like Girls," a pop song with direct lyrics about same-sex attraction that became a cultural moment. The accompanying music video went viral for its plainly worded statements of lesbian desire.

Kiyoko has now made her directorial debut by expanding that five-minute video into a feature-length film. The adaptation transforms the original narrative into a full exploration of adolescent emotion and identity, marking an unusual journey from pop song to cinema.

cards.headline: New Documentary Examines LGBTQ Community's Relationship With American Flag
cards.teaser: Jewelry designer and filmmaker Alexis Bittar directed a documentary about reclaiming the American flag for LGBTQ Americans.
cards.body:
Jewelry designer and filmmaker Alexis Bittar has released a documentary titled "Reclaim the Flag" that explores how LGBTQ Americans relate to national symbols. Bittar himself displays an American flag outside his Brooklyn home, which he shares with his husband and three children.

The film addresses the complex feelings many LGBTQ people experience toward patriotic imagery, particularly given its use by those who have opposed their rights. Bittar said some potential participants were hesitant to participate in the documentary, reflecting the sensitivity around the subject.

cards.headline: UFC Held Fight Event at White House
cards.teaser: Rolling Stone covered a UFC fight event called Freedom 250 held at the White House during the Trump administration.
cards.body:
The Ultimate Fighting Championship held an event at the White House called Freedom 250, which Rolling Stone described as a surreal spectacle. The magazine sent photographers and reporters to document the event, which marked an unusual intersection of combat sports and presidential politics.

The event represents part of a relationship between UFC and the Trump administration. Rolling Stone characterized the White House cage fights as blending entertainment, politics, and mixed martial arts in an unprecedented venue.

cards.headline: Patton Oswalt Open to Ratatouille Sequel Under Right Conditions
cards.teaser: The voice actor behind the rat chef said he would return for a sequel only if it serves the story rather than financial motives.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Patton Oswalt, who voiced the rat chef Remy in the 2007 Pixar film Ratatouille, said he would be interested in a sequel but only if it avoids being what he called a money grab. Oswalt stated that many sequels are inorganic, suggesting any follow-up to the Oscar-winning film would need creative justification.

Pixar has not franchised Ratatouille despite returning to other properties with Toy Story 5, Incredibles 3, Monsters Inc. 3, and Coco 2. Director Brad Bird's original film about a rat pursuing culinary dreams in Paris won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and became a critical favorite, though it has remained a standalone story in the Pixar catalog.

---

Note: The additional source material provided is about unrelated topics (EU regulation of Meta's WhatsApp and a Dutch court artist's AI copyright case). Since it contains no information about Patton Oswalt or Ratatouille, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: The Sphere to Present Rocky Horror Picture Show in 2027
cards.teaser: The Las Vegas venue will screen the cult classic film, following its earlier presentation of The Wizard of Oz.
cards.body:
The Sphere entertainment venue in Las Vegas announced it will present The Rocky Horror Picture Show in 2027. The cult film will receive treatment similar to the venue's earlier screening of The Wizard of Oz, using the massive immersive screen technology to present the classic movie.

The Rocky Horror Picture Show has maintained a devoted following since its 1975 release, with fans attending interactive midnight screenings for decades. The Sphere's technology offers a new way to experience the film, which tells the story of a couple encountering a bizarre household during a rainstorm.

cards.headline: Rush Draws New Young Audiences During Forum Comeback Shows
cards.teaser: The Canadian rock band attracted a fresh generation of fans during recent performances with a substitute drummer.
cards.body:
Rush performed at the Forum with a substitute drummer, attracting what one writer described as an unexpected young hipster audience in 2026. The Canadian rock trio, whose members are in their fifties, appears to be experiencing a cultural resurgence among younger music fans who typically favor indie bands.

The comeback shows marked a return for the band known for hits spanning multiple decades. A new generation has discovered Rush's progressive rock catalog, elevating the group to what some are calling the cool kids' choice in rock music this year, surpassing younger indie acts in cultural cachet among certain listeners.

hero.headline: Five arrested for alleged plot to attack UFC event at White House
hero.body:
Five individuals have been arrested and charged with plotting to attack a UFC event at the White House, the Department of Justice announced. Officials alleged that the plotters discussed sending explosive-loaded drones to the event and shooting people who fled.

The arrests represent a serious security threat to a public event at the executive mansion. The UFC event at the White House marks an unusual venue for the mixed martial arts organization, though the source material does not specify when the event was scheduled to take place or whether it has been canceled or postponed in light of the alleged plot.

The alleged conspirators reportedly planned a coordinated attack using both aerial and ground tactics. According to officials, the group discussed deploying drones loaded with explosives to target the event venue while also planning to open fire on attendees attempting to escape. The Department of Justice did not release the identities of those arrested or specify what charges they face.

The investigation and arrests underscore ongoing concerns about security threats to high-profile government venues and events. The White House has hosted various sporting and entertainment events over the years, typically requiring extensive security screening and planning. The alleged plot involving drone technology reflects evolving security challenges faced by law enforcement and Secret Service personnel responsible for protecting the executive mansion and its grounds.

The Department of Justice has not provided additional details about how authorities uncovered the alleged plot, whether the suspects had acquired explosives or weapons, or how far advanced the planning had progressed before the arrests were made.

cards.headline: Senate advances bipartisan housing bill after GOP dispute
cards.teaser: The Senate voted 87-8 to consider legislation that includes limits on institutional investors buying single-family homes.
cards.body:
The Senate voted 87-8 to consider a bipartisan housing bill after months of disagreement between House and Senate Republicans. The version ultimately agreed upon by both chambers includes language to limit the ability of institutional investors to buy up single-family homes, a provision House Republicans had fought to include.

Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina, a Republican, played a role in brokering the agreement between the two chambers. The legislation represents a compromise after extended negotiations within the GOP over how to address housing affordability and availability concerns.

cards.headline: Trump to attend dinner at Versailles celebrating US 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: French President Emmanuel Macron will host President Trump at the Palace of Versailles for a dinner marking America's 250th birthday.
cards.body: French President Emmanuel Macron will host President Trump at the Palace of Versailles on Wednesday to mark the 250th anniversary of American independence. Macron's office confirmed the dinner to the Associated Press on Saturday. The event at the historic palace outside Paris serves as a diplomatic gesture celebrating the milestone birthday of the United States and represents a symbol of Franco-American friendship.

cards.headline: White House dismisses George Conway impeachment campaign ad
cards.teaser: The White House responded to congressional candidate George Conway's campaign advertisement promising to impeach President Trump.
cards.body:
The White House criticized Democratic congressional candidate George Conway on Tuesday for airing a campaign advertisement in which he pledges to impeach President Trump if elected to the House of Representatives. Conway, a longtime Trump critic, has made impeachment a central focus of his New York congressional campaign.

White House officials responded to the ad by dismissing Conway's candidacy and attacking his credibility as a political figure.

cards.headline: FDA approves third over-the-counter naloxone nasal spray
cards.teaser: The agency approved Rextovy, a 4 milligram naloxone nasal spray, for emergency treatment of opioid overdose.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration approved a third over-the-counter version of naloxone nasal spray, a move the agency said could save lives and reduce costs. The FDA approved Rextovy, a 4 milligram naloxone nasal spray for emergency treatment of opioid overdose.

Consumers may purchase the spray directly in pharmacies, convenience stores and online without a prescription. Naloxone is a medication used to reverse opioid overdoses by blocking the effects of opioids in the body.

cards.headline: Florida sues TikTok for alleged violation of child safety law
cards.teaser: Attorney General Ashley Moody filed a lawsuit alleging the platform violates a state law banning children under 14 from social media.
cards.body:
Florida sued TikTok on Monday, alleging the platform violates a state law restricting social media access for minors. The law bans children under 14 from all social media platforms and requires parental consent for 15 and 16-year-olds to create accounts. Attorney General James Uthmeier led the lawsuit.

Uthmeier accused TikTok of exposing children to harmful sexual content and addictive features including unlimited scrolling and push notifications designed to extend screen time. He cited evidence that some children spend six, seven, eight or more hours daily on the platform, stating the state aims to help kids reclaim their lives.

cards.headline: Trump-backed Collins wins Georgia Senate Republican runoff
cards.teaser: Rep. Mike Collins defeated former college football coach Derek Dooley to secure the Republican nomination to face Sen. Jon Ossoff.
cards.body:
Rep. Mike Collins defeated former college football coach Derek Dooley in Georgia's Republican Senate runoff on Tuesday, securing the party's nomination to challenge Democrat Jon Ossoff in November's general election. Trump's last-minute endorsement boosted Collins over Dooley in the race.

The victory marks another win for Trump's endorsement power in Georgia's 2026 primary elections. Collins will transition from his House seat to pursue the Senate race against the incumbent Ossoff in what is expected to be competitive.
